# Was the FBI's NCIC crime database hacked?

**Not established.** CNN and NBC News, each citing two people briefed, report the FBI is investigating an apparent breach. The FBI has not commented, and no one has said what, if anything, was reached.

Incident: FBI crime database (NCIC) intrusion, reported Nov 20, 2026. Also reported as the NCIC breach and the FBI crime database hack. First published Nov 20, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 12:10 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the FBI, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Nation-level potential. NCIC is used by more than 100,000 criminal justice partners nationwide. No source says what was reached, so this is the worst case, not a known impact.
- Who is affected: Potentially police and courts that rely on NCIC, and people with records in it. No source says whose records, if any, were reached, and there is no notice for the public to act on.

### Known so far

- CNN and NBC News, each citing their own sources, report the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of NCIC.
- NCIC is the FBI-run database police nationwide use for warrants, stolen property and other records.
- The FBI has not commented on the CNN or NBC News reports.
- A separate breach hit the FBI jobs site in September; the FBI blamed a contractor's missed patch.

### Not known yet

- Whether the FBI confirms the breach. Both reports call it 'apparent' and rest on unnamed people briefed on the matter.
- What part of NCIC was reached, how the intruders got in, and who they are.
- Whether any records were copied or changed.
- Whether it is linked to this week's outages or the September jobs-site breach. No source says so.
- Whether NCIC service for police was interrupted.
